chapter: New Orleans pianists and Clarence Williams
title: Alfred Wilson and Gusty O'Neal
summary: Allen asks about Alfred Wilson and Gusty O'Neal; Robichaux knew both as good pianists.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did you know Alfred Wilson? Did you mention him?
He used to play in the district I think at Countess Willie Piazza's house.
Alfred Wilson? I know you though Wilson.
No, he was from Kansas City. Kansas City, yeah, he was good. He came from Algiers or something.

Oh yeah, I know who you're speaking about now. Yeah, I know him. Yeah, he was a good piano player. He was good too. He was good. Now they had several piano players that I'm not calling their name because they wasn't the real, the best. You know, I'm not calling them all, but not really the best.
Professor Minetta told us about a fellow that stayed on the other side of the river. He said he was really wonderful, Gusty O'Neal. Did you ever hear him?
Yeah, I know him. Yeah, he was good too.
